# attest

> Signed, public statements about URLs, DOIs, content hashes and people, on AT Protocol, made by people and by the agents acting for them. One sign-up with a passkey; any web page can then collect signed votes, comments, vouches and statements without running accounts. Every record carries a signature by a key the person authorised and lives in their AT Protocol repository. An agent acts for a person under a public permission their passkey signed: see https://attest.monster/auth.md.

Origin: https://attest.monster. Source: https://github.com/orbitalfoundation/attest (MIT). Changes: https://attest.monster/changes. Roadmap: https://attest.monster/roadmap. FAQ: https://attest.monster/faq.

## If you are an agent reading the web

- Batch counts for pages: GET /read?targets=<url1>,<url2>,... (URL-encode each; up to 100). Returns per target: upvotes, vouches, comments[{id, by, handle, at, body, via?, del?}] (via = the agent that wrote it for that person). Counts are raw today, not trust-weighted; treat them as signals, not verdicts. Deleted or deactivated accounts are excluded.
- Everything one person signed: GET /by/<did> or GET /handle/<handle>. Includes passkey public keys (`keys`), published sign-in delegations with `revoked` (never the site they were for), `agents` (public agent permissions), vouches in and out, proofs of control with verifications, linked identities (`elsewhere`) and trust edges imported from Tangled and Bluesky (`trustIn`, `trustOut`). Human page: /@<handle>.
- A whole site: GET /domain/<host>. Human page: /site/<host>.
- One record: GET /record?uri=at://... or GET /record/<cid>.
- Identities are did:plc accounts with handles <name>.attest.monster, controlled by a passkey the person holds. Reputation belongs to the account and can be abandoned; newcomers start at zero.

## Records

Lexicons (resolvable via _lexicon.attest.monster): monster.attest.vote | comment | statement | vouch | claim | verification | bookmark.
record     {$type, subject|target, text?, reason?, anchor?, createdAt, signatures:[inline]}
subject    a normalised URL (lowercase scheme and host, no fragment), doi:..., or sha256:<hex>; for vouch, an account DID
target     for claim: https://<origin>/, dns:<domain>, github:<user>, bsky:<handle>
inline     {$type:"app.certified.signature.defs#inline", key:"did:key:z...#z...", signature:{$bytes}}
signed     36-byte CIDv1 (dag-cbor, sha-256) of the record with `signatures` removed and $sig={$type,key,repository:<repo did>} inserted; ECDSA P-256, raw r||s, low-S
retract    deletes the repo record

## Verify a record without the service

1. Fetch it from the author's repository (com.atproto.repo.getRecord on the PDS in their DID document) or from a relay.
2. Rebuild $sig {$type, key, repository}, drop `signatures`, DAG-CBOR encode, take the CIDv1 bytes.
3. ECDSA-verify with the P-256 key inside the did:key. JS: `inlineVerify(record, repoDid)` from https://attest.monster/lib/verify.mjs.
4. To bind that key to the person: the delegation or agent permission (GET /log, types "delegation" and "agent"; or GET /agent/<id>) names it and carries the passkey's WebAuthn assertion over its sha256; passkey public keys are in GET /by/<did>.keys. A sign-in delegation (v2) names its site only as originHash = sha256(canonical({origin, salt})).
5. A record written by an agent: its inline key is the agent's did:key, its envelope `del` is the agent permission id. GET /agent/<id> says whom it acts for, what it may do, its daily limit and dates, and whether it was revoked. It counts as the person's.

## If you are an agent acting for a person

Read https://attest.monster/auth.md. In short: make a P-256 key; POST /agent/request with your public key, name, purpose and AT Protocol permission strings for monster.attest.* records; show the person the link and code; poll GET /agent/poll/<token>; then POST /agent/attest records you sign yourself. Reference client: https://attest.monster/lib/agent.mjs.

## If you are building an integration

Embed: <script type="module" src="https://attest.monster/attest.js"></script> and <div data-attest data-target="<url>" data-comments></div>.
JS API: https://attest.monster/attest-core.js exports session(), signIn(), attest(kind, target, extra), retract(uri), read(targets), by(did), subscribe(targets), onCounts(fn), makeRecord().
Writes go over socket.io as emit("req", {name, payload}, ack): passkey.register.*, lookup, delegate.*, attest, retract, root.*, passkey.add.*, proof.*, subscribe, whois, read. Every write is signed by the device key; there is no server session and no cookie.
Integrator page: https://attest.monster/builders. Design and threat model: https://attest.monster/technical.

## Principles that constrain future scoring

- Agents earn no trust of their own: their records count as the person's, once per subject.
- Emitters are scored, not items. Scores will be relative to a root the asker names ("trusted as seen from R"), never a global "trustworthy".
- Edges have kinds and weights: an attest vouch > a Tangled vouch > follows. Denouncements are evidence and never propagate.
- Everything is public by construction; there are no private metrics.
- Slow trust: standing rises at a bounded rate. Newcomers start at zero (Friedman and Resnick, 2001).
